rules.statement: A surety's liability is limited to paying the principal debtor if they fail to do so, and a general renunciation of suretyship rights must be specific or declared by a lawyer for it to be valid.
rules.supporting_quote: "The 'payment' here referred to is clearly the payment by the company to the plaintiff. Any liability undertaken by a surety must be construed strictly and in a sense least burdensome to the surety, and when the defendant in the first clause agrees that, if there shall be the whole or any part of the said monies due and payable at the expiration of twelve months, he shall, and will pay the same to the plaintiff, the only conclusion is that he undertakes to pay if the company shall not have paid within the period mentioned, and that thus he makes himself liable no more and no less than as surety."
